controls.label: Color + brightness
controls.qualification: The star's color, darker where TESS saw it dimmer (contrast drawn stronger) · February and March 2020, mapped in this project
controls.notes: TYC 1987-509-1 in its own color, darker where its light in TESS's images of February and March 2020 says it was darker. As the star turned once in 9.04 days its light rose and fell by 0.83%. The light repeats every 4.52 days, half the catalogued rotation period, and the star is taken to turn once in two of them. The contrast is drawn far stronger than it is, so the eye can see it: the darkest part gives 3.9% less light than the brightest, and is drawn as a much darker tone of the star's own hue; the Brightness map's scale has the measured values. The longitudes of the darker and brighter parts are measured. Their latitudes and shapes are not: they are the smoothest that reproduce the light. No change of color is drawn, because none is measured. Spots come and go within weeks or months: this is the star then. The darkening toward the edge is the Color dataset's limb law, drawn 1.5 times as strong.

controls.label: Brightness map
controls.qualification: Mapped in this project · TESS mission light curve, sector 22
controls.notes: Where the star's surface was darker and brighter in TESS sector 22, worked out in this project from how its light rose and fell by 0.83% as it turned once in 9.04 days. The light curve is the mission's own; the criteria of Holcomb et al. (2022, ApJ 936, 138) decide that it shows the star turning, and starry finds the map that reproduces it. The longitudes of the dark and bright regions are fixed by the data; their latitudes are not. The light repeats every 4.52 days, half the rotation period the catalogues print for the star: two groups of spots on opposite sides do that. The map is made at the tilt the page draws the star with, 67°.
controls.legendNote: Darker: dimmer than the star's mean surface; white: brighter. Black line: 67° S; the star never shows us what lies below it.

controls.label: Color
controls.qualification: Color from Gaia's spectrum of the star; darkening toward the edge from a model atmosphere. The disc itself is unresolved.
controls.notes: The color of the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum. The darkening toward the edge is the quadratic law Claret & Bloemen (2011), A&A 529, A75 compute from ATLAS model atmospheres for the Johnson V band at 5,340 K and log g 4.55 (u1 0.563, u2 0.191): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used. The spin axis's direction on the sky is a display convention.

controls.label: Radial field
controls.qualification: Mapped in this project · CFHT ESPaDOnS spectra, Apr 2015
controls.notes: The star's large-scale magnetic field in Apr 2015, reconstructed in this project from 15 archived ESPaDOnS spectra with the published codes LSDpy and ZDIpy. It is this project's reduction, not a published map. Folsom, C. P. et al., arXiv:1711.08636 map the same run with a mean field of 25 G; this map has 22 G.
controls.legendNote: Red: field pointing out of the star; blue: into it. Black line: 67° S; the star never shows us what lies below it.
